scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service charge incurred 34 days ago, which is slightly outside the standard 30-day refund policy window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Scott Wagner and I'm 42. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Scott, thank you for reaching out. I understand how frustrating it can be to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the last four digits of the payment method used?
Sure, the email is scott.wagner@email.com and the card ends in 4492.

Thank you, Scott. I have located your account. I see the cancellation was processed on day 34, and per our 'Service Terms Section 4.2', refunds are typically restricted to requests made within 30 days of the transaction date. However, given your account history is in good standing, I would like to see if I can make an exception for you.
I appreciate that. It really was just an oversight because I was away for work. It's only a few days over, so I'm hoping you can help.

I completely understand. I have reviewed the transaction details and, as a one-time courtesy for a loyal customer, I am authorized to override the 30-day limit. I have processed a full refund of $89.99 to your card ending in 4492. It should appear in your statement within 3-5 business days.
That is fantastic news, thank you so much for your help with this!
You are very welcome, Scott! I'm glad we could get that sorted out for you. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: Agent verified account details and applied a one-time courtesy exception to the 30-day refund policy, successfully issuing a full refund.
